definition_en: An art style showing subjects through geometric shapes and multiple viewpoints.
example1_en: The quiz had a short question about the development of cubism.
example1_zh: 小测里有一道关于立体主义的发展的简答题。
example2_en: A campus survey used the development of cubism to explain a pattern in the humanities.
example2_zh: 一项校园调查用立体主义的发展来解释人文学科中的一种模式。
collocations: the development of cubism｜立体主义的发展 ; analytical cubism｜分析立体主义 ; synthetic cubism｜综合立体主义
tip_zh: 通常不可数；cubist 可指立体派艺术家或作形容词。

meanings_zh: n. 参议员
definition_en: A member of a senate, a lawmaking body
example1_en: The textbook introduces a senior senator in the first chapter.
example1_zh: 教材在第一章介绍了资深参议员。
example2_en: The listening passage defines the discussion around a senior senator.
example2_zh: 这段听力材料围绕资深参议员展开说明。
collocations: elect a senator｜选举参议员 ; serve as a senator｜担任参议员 ; a senior senator｜资深参议员
tip_zh: senator是参议员；senate指参议院。

meanings_zh: v. 使湿透；使淋透
definition_en: To make someone or something completely wet
example1_en: Before Friday's seminar, our group has to drench someone with water.
example1_zh: 周五研讨课之前，我们小组必须用水把某人浇透。
example2_en: A lecture on the natural sciences showed why researchers drench someone with water before they publish.
example2_zh: 关于自然科学的讲座说明了研究者为什么在发表之前要用水把某人浇透。
collocations: get drenched｜被淋透 ; drenched in sweat｜汗流浃背 ; drench someone with water｜用水把某人浇透
tip_zh: 强调完全湿透；常用被动形式be drenched。

meanings_zh: n. 冷杉；冷杉木
definition_en: An evergreen tree with needle-shaped leaves, or its wood.
example1_en: The quiz had a short question about a fir tree.
example1_zh: 小测里有一道关于一棵冷杉的简答题。
example2_en: Students compared two sources that both discuss a fir tree.
example2_zh: 学生比较了两份都讨论一棵冷杉的材料。
collocations: a fir tree｜一棵冷杉 ; a fir forest｜冷杉林 ; fir needles｜冷杉针叶
tip_zh: fir是冷杉；fur才是毛皮，两词同音。

meanings_zh: v. 间接提及；暗指
definition_en: to refer to something without mentioning it directly
example1_en: The professor asked us to allude to a problem.
example1_zh: 教授让我们间接提及问题。
example2_en: The reading asks you to allude to a problem and then check a second source.
example2_zh: 这篇阅读要求你间接提及问题，然后再核对第二个来源。
collocations: allude to a problem｜间接提及问题 ; allude to the past｜隐约谈及过去
tip_zh: 固定用allude to，不直接接宾语；勿混elude。

meanings_zh: n. 无记名投票；投票表决 | n. 选票 | v. 组织投票；投票
definition_en: A process of voting, usually in secret. | A paper or electronic form used to record a vote. | To ask people to vote, or to vote yourself.
example1_en: The seminar spent a few minutes on secret ballot.
example1_zh: 研讨课花了几分钟讨论无记名投票。
example2_en: Students compared two sources that both discuss secret ballot.
example2_zh: 学生比较了两份都讨论无记名投票的材料。
collocations: secret ballot｜无记名投票 ; ballot paper｜选票 ; ballot box｜投票箱 ; hold a ballot｜举行投票
tip_zh: ballot侧重投票程序或选票；by secret ballot指无记名投票。

meanings_zh: n. 鱼雷 | v. 彻底破坏；使失败
definition_en: an underwater weapon that propels itself towards a target | to deliberately cause a plan or agreement to fail
example1_en: The quiz had a short question about torpedo tube.
example1_zh: 小测里有一道关于鱼雷发射管的简答题。
example2_en: The listening passage defines the discussion around torpedo tube.
example2_zh: 这段听力材料围绕鱼雷发射管展开说明。
collocations: launch a torpedo｜发射鱼雷 ; torpedo tube｜鱼雷发射管 ; torpedo a plan｜破坏计划
tip_zh: 鱼雷是torpedo；水雷是mine。复数为torpedoes。

meanings_zh: n. 输送管道 | n. 供应渠道；开发流程
definition_en: A long pipe carrying liquids or gas between places. | A system through which things are supplied or developed.
example1_en: The textbook introduces a gas pipeline in the first chapter.
example1_zh: 教材在第一章介绍了天然气管道。
example2_en: In the lecture on technological change, everyone remembered the example of a gas pipeline.
example2_zh: 在关于技术变革的讲座里，大家都记得天然气管道这个例子。
collocations: a gas pipeline｜天然气管道 ; an oil pipeline｜输油管道 ; in the pipeline｜在筹备中 ; a development pipeline｜开发流程
tip_zh: in the pipeline常指项目正在筹备或推进中。

meanings_zh: n. 男爵 | n. 行业巨头；大亨
definition_en: A man holding a low-ranking title of nobility. | A wealthy person with great power in a particular industry.
example1_en: Our professor circled a media baron on the slide.
example1_zh: 教授在幻灯片上圈出了传媒大亨。
example2_en: The author returns to a media baron when explaining the conclusion.
example2_zh: 作者在解释结论时又回到了传媒大亨。
collocations: a media baron｜传媒大亨 ; a press baron｜报业大亨 ; an oil baron｜石油大亨
tip_zh: 本义为男爵；行业名词加baron可指该行业大亨。

meanings_zh: adv. 傲慢地；自大地
definition_en: In a way that suggests superiority to other people.
example1_en: The professor told us to arrogantly dismiss and then compare notes.
example1_zh: 教授让我们傲慢地否定，然后比较笔记。
example2_en: The reading shows why a careful writer will arrogantly dismiss when the evidence is thin.
example2_zh: 这篇阅读说明，证据不足时，谨慎的作者会傲慢地否定。
collocations: behave arrogantly｜举止傲慢 ; speak arrogantly｜说话傲慢 ; arrogantly dismiss｜傲慢地否定
tip_zh: 带贬义；自信地通常用confidently。

meanings_zh: v. 遵守；坚持 | v. 黏附；附着
definition_en: To follow a rule, belief, or agreement closely. | To stick firmly to a surface.
example1_en: Before Friday's seminar, our group has to adhere to guidelines.
example1_zh: 周五研讨课之前，我们小组必须遵循指导原则。
example2_en: The reading asks you to adhere to guidelines and then check a second source.
example2_zh: 这篇阅读要求你遵循指导原则，然后再核对第二个来源。
collocations: adhere to guidelines｜遵循指导原则 ; adhere to principles｜坚持原则 ; adhere to a surface｜黏附于表面
tip_zh: 两种常见义都用adhere to；to是介词。

meanings_zh: adj. 多石的；铺满石头的 | adj. 冷漠的；毫无表情的
definition_en: covered with or containing many stones | showing no warmth, sympathy, or emotion
example1_en: The textbook introduces stony ground in the first chapter.
example1_zh: 教材在第一章介绍了多石的土地。
example2_en: Students compared two sources that both discuss stony ground.
example2_zh: 学生比较了两份都讨论多石的土地的材料。
collocations: stony ground｜多石的土地 ; a stony path｜满是石头的小路 ; stony silence｜冷冰冰的沉默 ; a stony expression｜冷漠的表情
tip_zh: stony silence 指冷漠或不悦的沉默，并非普通安静。

meanings_zh: v. 使瘫痪；使麻痹 | v. 使停摆；使无法行动
definition_en: Make someone unable to move all or part of their body. | Prevent a system from functioning or a person from acting.
example1_en: I heard the lecturer paralyze transport during the example.
example1_zh: 我听到讲者在举例时使交通瘫痪。
example2_en: The passage says students who can paralyze transport follow the argument more easily.
example2_zh: 文章说，能够使交通瘫痪的学生更容易跟上论点。
collocations: paralyze transport｜使交通瘫痪 ; paralyzed by fear｜吓得无法动弹 ; partially paralyzed｜部分瘫痪
tip_zh: 美式拼写paralyze；英式通常写paralyse。

meanings_zh: n. 堂区；基层行政区 | n. 堂区全体居民
definition_en: A local church district, or a small administrative area. | The people living in a particular church district.
example1_en: Our professor circled parish church on the slide.
example1_zh: 教授在幻灯片上圈出了堂区教堂。
example2_en: In the lecture on social change, everyone remembered the example of parish church.
example2_zh: 在关于社会变迁的讲座里，大家都记得堂区教堂这个例子。
collocations: parish church｜堂区教堂 ; parish priest｜堂区神父 ; parish council｜堂区议会
tip_zh: 教会语境指堂区，比主教管辖的diocese小。

meanings_zh: n. 迷人魅力；华丽气质
definition_en: An exciting attractiveness associated with beauty, wealth, or fame.
example1_en: The quiz had a short question about Hollywood glamour.
example1_zh: 小测里有一道关于好莱坞式的华丽魅力的简答题。
example2_en: A campus survey used Hollywood glamour to explain a pattern in the humanities.
example2_zh: 一项校园调查用好莱坞式的华丽魅力来解释人文学科中的一种模式。
collocations: add glamour to｜为……增添魅力 ; the glamour of fame｜名声的光环 ; Hollywood glamour｜好莱坞式的华丽魅力
tip_zh: 通常不可数；美式也写glamor。

meanings_zh: n. 忧虑；担心 | n. 逮捕；拘捕
definition_en: Worry that something unpleasant may happen. | The act of catching and arresting someone suspected of a crime.
example1_en: Office hours began with a sense of apprehension.
example1_zh: 答疑从忧虑感开始。
example2_en: A campus survey used a sense of apprehension to explain a pattern in human behavior.
example2_zh: 一项校园调查用忧虑感来解释人类行为中的一种模式。
collocations: apprehension about｜对……的忧虑 ; a sense of apprehension｜忧虑感 ; with apprehension｜担忧地
tip_zh: 常指对未来的担忧，常接about；逮捕义较正式。

meanings_zh: v. 保护；保障 | n. 保护措施；保障
definition_en: To protect someone or something from harm or loss. | A measure that prevents harm, loss, or unfair treatment.
example1_en: The lab instructions say to safeguard rights.
example1_zh: 实验说明要求保障权利。
example2_en: A lecture on public institutions showed why researchers safeguard rights before they publish.
example2_zh: 关于公共制度的讲座说明了研究者为什么在发表之前要保障权利。
collocations: safeguard rights｜保障权利 ; safeguard personal information｜保护个人信息 ; a safeguard against fraud｜防范欺诈的措施
tip_zh: 动词常接权益等宾语；名词常接against表示防范对象。

meanings_zh: n. 穿透；渗透 | n. 市场渗透；普及程度
definition_en: The process of entering or passing through something. | The extent to which a product reaches a market.
example1_en: The quiz had a short question about water penetration.
example1_zh: 小测里有一道关于水分渗透的简答题。
example2_en: Students compared two sources that both discuss water penetration.
example2_zh: 学生比较了两份都讨论水分渗透的材料。
collocations: water penetration｜水分渗透 ; market penetration｜市场渗透 ; internet penetration｜互联网普及程度
tip_zh: 由penetrate派生；常用penetration of或into。

meanings_zh: n. 垮台；败落 | n. 失败的原因
definition_en: The loss of power, success, or social position. | Something that causes a person or organisation to fail.
example1_en: The textbook introduces lead to someone's downfall in the first chapter.
example1_zh: 教材在第一章介绍了导致某人垮台。
example2_en: The author returns to lead to someone's downfall when explaining the conclusion.
example2_zh: 作者在解释结论时又回到了导致某人垮台。
collocations: lead to someone's downfall｜导致某人垮台 ; bring about the downfall of｜促使……败落 ; prove to be someone's downfall｜最终成为某人失败的原因
tip_zh: 指垮台或败因；倾盆大雨应说downpour。

meanings_zh: n. 愤慨；义愤 | v. 使愤慨；激怒 | n. 骇人行径；暴行
definition_en: Intense anger caused by something deeply unfair or wrong | To make someone extremely angry through unacceptable behaviour | An act that is shockingly wrong or unacceptable
example1_en: Our professor circled public outrage on the slide.
example1_zh: 教授在幻灯片上圈出了公众的愤慨。
example2_en: The listening passage defines the discussion around public outrage.
example2_zh: 这段听力材料围绕公众的愤慨展开说明。
collocations: public outrage｜公众的愤慨 ; spark outrage｜激起公愤 ; express outrage｜表达愤慨 ; an outrage against humanity｜反人类暴行
tip_zh: 表愤慨通常不可数；an outrage指骇人行径。

meanings_zh: n. 恳求；请求 | n. 认罪或不认罪的答辩
definition_en: An urgent, emotional request for something. | A formal statement admitting or denying guilt in court.
example1_en: The seminar spent a few minutes on a guilty plea.
example1_zh: 研讨课花了几分钟讨论认罪答辩。
example2_en: The listening passage defines the discussion around a guilty plea.
example2_zh: 这段听力材料围绕认罪答辩展开说明。
collocations: a plea for help｜恳求帮助 ; make a plea｜提出恳求 ; a guilty plea｜认罪答辩 ; enter a plea｜正式作出答辩
tip_zh: plea for后接所求之物；plea to后接请求对象。

meanings_zh: v. 宣布非法；禁止 | n. 逃犯；亡命之徒
definition_en: to make an activity illegal | a criminal who lives outside the law
example1_en: The lab instructions say to outlaw a practice.
example1_zh: 实验说明要求禁止某种做法。
example2_en: The reading asks you to outlaw a practice and then check a second source.
example2_zh: 这篇阅读要求你禁止某种做法，然后再核对第二个来源。
collocations: outlaw a practice｜禁止某种做法 ; outlaw discrimination｜宣布歧视行为非法 ; a notorious outlaw｜臭名昭著的逃犯
tip_zh: 作动词时直接接被禁止的行为或事物。

meanings_zh: adj. 公正的；不偏不倚的
definition_en: Treating all sides fairly without favouring anyone.
example1_en: Office hours began with impartial advice.
example1_zh: 答疑从公正的建议开始。
example2_en: The author returns to impartial advice when explaining the conclusion.
example2_zh: 作者在解释结论时又回到了公正的建议。
collocations: impartial advice｜公正的建议 ; impartial judge｜公正的法官 ; remain impartial｜保持公正
tip_zh: partial 可表示偏袒的；impartial 表示不偏袒。

meanings_zh: n. 分歧；差异 | n. 分叉；分离
definition_en: A difference between opinions, approaches, or developments. | Movement apart in different directions from a common point.
example1_en: I copied growing divergence into my lecture notes.
example1_zh: 我把不断扩大的差异抄进了课堂笔记。
example2_en: The reading connects growing divergence with a larger point about academic research.
example2_zh: 这篇阅读把不断扩大的差异和关于学术研究的一个更大的问题联系起来。
collocations: divergence of opinion｜意见分歧 ; divergence between｜……之间的差异 ; growing divergence｜不断扩大的差异
tip_zh: 常用between连接差异双方；动词为diverge。

meanings_zh: v. 放大 | v. 夸大；加剧
definition_en: To make something appear larger, especially through a lens. | To make something seem more important or become more serious.
example1_en: The professor asked us to magnify an image.
example1_zh: 教授让我们放大图像。
example2_en: A lecture on the natural sciences showed why researchers magnify an image before they publish.
example2_zh: 关于自然科学的讲座说明了研究者为什么在发表之前要放大图像。
collocations: magnify an image｜放大图像 ; magnify a problem｜加剧问题 ; magnifying glass｜放大镜
tip_zh: 既可指视觉放大，也可指夸大问题或加剧影响。

meanings_zh: adj. 坦率的；直言不讳的 | adj. 抓拍的；非摆拍的
definition_en: Honest and direct, even about uncomfortable subjects. | Photographed naturally without being asked to pose.
example1_en: The seminar spent a few minutes on a candid assessment.
example1_zh: 研讨课花了几分钟讨论坦率的评估。
example2_en: In the lecture on social change, everyone remembered the example of a candid assessment.
example2_zh: 在关于社会变迁的讲座里，大家都记得坦率的评估这个例子。
collocations: a candid assessment｜坦率的评估 ; be candid about｜坦率谈论 ; a candid photograph｜抓拍照片
tip_zh: 谈人或言论指坦率；谈照片指非摆拍。

meanings_zh: v. 悲痛；哀悼 | v. 使悲伤
definition_en: To feel deep sadness, especially after someone's death | To cause someone deep sadness
example1_en: In office hours we practiced how to grieve over a loss.
example1_zh: 答疑时我们练习如何为失去而悲伤。
example2_en: A lecture on human behavior showed why researchers grieve over a loss before they publish.
example2_zh: 关于人类行为的讲座说明了研究者为什么在发表之前要为失去而悲伤。
collocations: grieve for someone｜为某人哀痛 ; grieve over a loss｜为失去而悲伤 ; time to grieve｜哀悼的时间
tip_zh: grieve for常接逝者；grieve over常接损失或不幸。

meanings_zh: adj. 无形的；难以衡量的
definition_en: Not physically touchable or easily measured, but still real or valuable
example1_en: The seminar spent a few minutes on intangible benefits.
example1_zh: 研讨课花了几分钟讨论无形的益处。
example2_en: In the lecture on economic policy, everyone remembered the example of intangible benefits.
example2_zh: 在关于经济政策的讲座里，大家都记得无形的益处这个例子。
collocations: intangible benefits｜无形的益处 ; intangible assets｜无形资产 ; intangible cultural heritage｜非物质文化遗产
tip_zh: 不仅指摸不到，也指价值等难以量化。

meanings_zh: v. 唤起；引起
definition_en: to bring a feeling, memory or image into someone's mind
example1_en: The professor asked us to evoke memories.
example1_zh: 教授让我们唤起回忆。
example2_en: Careful notes from the talk include a reminder to evoke memories.
example2_zh: 听课笔记里写着要记得唤起回忆。
collocations: evoke memories｜唤起回忆 ; evoke emotions｜激起情感 ; evoke an image｜唤起画面 ; evoke sympathy｜引起同情
tip_zh: 直接接情感、回忆等宾语，不加of。

meanings_zh: adj. 潜在的；未来可能的
definition_en: Likely or hoping to become something in the future.
example1_en: The quiz had a short question about prospective students.
example1_zh: 小测里有一道关于有意入学的学生的简答题。
example2_en: Students compared two sources that both discuss prospective students.
example2_zh: 学生比较了两份都讨论有意入学的学生的材料。
collocations: prospective students｜有意入学的学生 ; prospective buyers｜潜在买家 ; prospective employers｜潜在雇主
tip_zh: 常放名词前；勿与perspective“视角”混淆。

meanings_zh: n. 搬家工人；搬家公司 | n. 推动者；发起者
definition_en: A person or company paid to move furniture and belongings. | Someone who actively helps make a change or project happen.
example1_en: The quiz had a short question about a prime mover.
example1_zh: 小测里有一道关于主要推动者的简答题。
example2_en: The listening passage defines the discussion around a prime mover.
example2_zh: 这段听力材料围绕主要推动者展开说明。
collocations: hire movers｜雇搬家工人 ; a prime mover｜主要推动者 ; movers and shakers｜有影响力的人物
tip_zh: 搬家工人义多见于美式；prime mover指主要推动者。

meanings_zh: n. 选区居民；选民 | n. 组成部分；成分 | adj. 组成的；构成的
definition_en: a person living in an area represented by an elected official | one of the parts or substances that form something | forming part of a larger whole
example1_en: Office hours began with a major constituent.
example1_zh: 答疑从主要成分开始。
example2_en: The author returns to a major constituent when explaining the conclusion.
example2_zh: 作者在解释结论时又回到了主要成分。
collocations: local constituents｜当地选区居民 ; constituent parts｜组成部分 ; a major constituent｜主要成分
tip_zh: 选民义可含未投票的选区居民；成分义近component。

meanings_zh: adj. 熟悉的；通晓的
definition_en: Familiar with a subject and able to discuss it
example1_en: Office hours began with conversant with.
example1_zh: 答疑从熟悉……的开始。
example2_en: The listening passage defines the discussion around conversant with.
example2_zh: 这段听力材料围绕熟悉……的展开说明。
collocations: conversant with｜熟悉……的 ; fully conversant with｜完全熟悉……的 ; conversant with procedures｜熟悉流程的
tip_zh: 常用be conversant with，表示熟悉某领域，并非有交情。

meanings_zh: n. 语音学
definition_en: The study of speech sounds and how people produce them.
example1_en: Office hours began with articulatory phonetics.
example1_zh: 答疑从发音语音学开始。
example2_en: A campus survey used articulatory phonetics to explain a pattern in academic research.
example2_zh: 一项校园调查用发音语音学来解释学术研究中的一种模式。
collocations: study phonetics｜学习语音学 ; articulatory phonetics｜发音语音学 ; acoustic phonetics｜声学语音学
tip_zh: 虽以-s结尾，作学科名时通常接单数谓语。

meanings_zh: n. 仔细考虑；商议 | n. 从容审慎；不慌不忙
definition_en: Careful thought or discussion before making a decision. | A slow, careful, and intentional way of doing something.
example1_en: I copied after much deliberation into my lecture notes.
example1_zh: 我把经过反复考虑抄进了课堂笔记。
example2_en: In the lecture on academic research, everyone remembered the example of after much deliberation.
example2_zh: 在关于学术研究的讲座里，大家都记得经过反复考虑这个例子。
collocations: after much deliberation｜经过反复考虑 ; careful deliberation｜慎重考虑 ; with deliberation｜从容审慎地
tip_zh: 表商议过程可用复数deliberations；勿一律译为故意。

meanings_zh: n. 限制；制约因素 | n. 拘束；克制
definition_en: Something that limits what you can do. | Control that prevents free or natural behaviour.
example1_en: The quiz had a short question about a constraint on growth.
example1_zh: 小测里有一道关于对增长的制约的简答题。
example2_en: In the lecture on economic policy, everyone remembered the example of a constraint on growth.
example2_zh: 在关于经济政策的讲座里，大家都记得对增长的制约这个例子。
collocations: time constraints｜时间限制 ; financial constraints｜财务限制 ; a constraint on growth｜对增长的制约 ; within budget constraints｜在预算限制内
tip_zh: 常用复数constraints；对……的限制用on。

meanings_zh: n. 繁殖；增殖 | n. 传播；扩散 | n. 波的传播
definition_en: The production of new plants or other living organisms. | The spreading of ideas, information, or beliefs. | The movement of waves or signals through a medium.
example1_en: The seminar spent a few minutes on plant propagation.
example1_zh: 研讨课花了几分钟讨论植物繁殖。
example2_en: In the lecture on the natural sciences, everyone remembered the example of plant propagation.
example2_zh: 在关于自然科学的讲座里，大家都记得植物繁殖这个例子。
collocations: plant propagation｜植物繁殖 ; propagation by cuttings｜扦插繁殖 ; wave propagation｜波的传播 ; propagation of ideas｜思想传播
tip_zh: 通常不可数；可用于植物繁殖、信息传播及波传播。

meanings_zh: v. 阻止；使打消念头
definition_en: To discourage an action by making it seem difficult or risky.
example1_en: I heard the lecturer deter crime during the example.
example1_zh: 我听到讲者在举例时遏制犯罪。
example2_en: The passage says students who can deter crime follow the argument more easily.
example2_zh: 文章说，能够遏制犯罪的学生更容易跟上论点。
collocations: deter someone from doing something｜阻止某人做某事 ; deter crime｜遏制犯罪 ; deter potential customers｜使潜在顾客却步
tip_zh: 用deter sb from doing；过去式为deterred。

meanings_zh: v. 搁置；暂缓 | v. 把…放上架子
definition_en: to stop considering or working on something for now | to put something on a shelf
example1_en: I heard the lecturer shelve a plan during the example.
example1_zh: 我听到讲者在举例时搁置计划。
example2_en: A lecture on economic policy showed why researchers shelve a plan before they publish.
example2_zh: 关于经济政策的讲座说明了研究者为什么在发表之前要搁置计划。
collocations: shelve a plan｜搁置计划 ; shelve a proposal｜暂缓考虑提案 ; shelve books｜把书放上书架
tip_zh: shelve作动词；shelf是名词，复数为shelves。

meanings_zh: v. 大量侵扰；成群寄生于
definition_en: To live in a place in large, harmful or unwanted groups.
example1_en: I heard the lecturer infest crops during the example.
example1_zh: 我听到讲者在举例时侵害庄稼。
example2_en: The passage says students who can infest crops follow the argument more easily.
example2_zh: 文章说，能够侵害庄稼的学生更容易跟上论点。
collocations: be infested with rats｜老鼠成灾 ; infest crops｜侵害庄稼 ; insect-infested buildings｜虫害严重的建筑
tip_zh: 常用be infested with，主语是受虫鼠侵扰处。

meanings_zh: v. 是……的特征 | v. 描述……的特点
definition_en: To be a typical or distinguishing feature of something. | To describe the main qualities of someone or something.
example1_en: I heard the lecturer characterize something as during the example.
example1_zh: 我听到讲者在举例时将某事物描述为。
example2_en: The reading asks you to characterize something as and then check a second source.
example2_zh: 这篇阅读要求你将某事物描述为，然后再核对第二个来源。
collocations: be characterized by｜以……为特征 ; characterize something as｜将某事物描述为
tip_zh: 英式也拼characterise；被动式常接by。

meanings_zh: adj. 不稳固的；摇摇欲坠的 | adj. 不稳定的；岌岌可危的
definition_en: not securely positioned and likely to fall | uncertain and likely to become dangerous or unsuccessful
example1_en: The seminar spent a few minutes on a precarious position.
example1_zh: 研讨课花了几分钟讨论岌岌可危的处境。
example2_en: The listening passage defines the discussion around a precarious position.
example2_zh: 这段听力材料围绕岌岌可危的处境展开说明。
collocations: a precarious position｜岌岌可危的处境 ; precarious employment｜不稳定的就业 ; a precarious balance｜不稳固的平衡 ; precarious finances｜不稳定的财务状况
tip_zh: 不仅表示“不稳定”，还暗含随时出问题的风险。

meanings_zh: v. 施加；运用 | v. 使自己努力；尽力
definition_en: To apply force, influence, or authority. | To make a strong physical or mental effort.
example1_en: The lab instructions say to exert pressure on.
example1_zh: 实验说明要求向……施加压力。
example2_en: In the sample listening, the professor pauses to exert pressure on.
example2_zh: 在示例听力里，教授停下来向……施加压力。
collocations: exert pressure on｜向……施加压力 ; exert influence over｜对……施加影响 ; exert yourself｜使自己努力
tip_zh: 常接pressure、influence；exert oneself意为尽力。

meanings_zh: v. 回忆起；记起
definition_en: remember something from the past, sometimes with effort
example1_en: The professor asked us to recollect doing something.
example1_zh: 教授让我们记得做过某事。
example2_en: A lecture on academic research showed why researchers recollect doing something before they publish.
example2_zh: 关于学术研究的讲座说明了研究者为什么在发表之前要记得做过某事。
collocations: clearly recollect｜清楚地记得 ; recollect doing something｜记得做过某事 ; as far as I recollect｜据我回忆
tip_zh: 比remember正式；用recollect doing，不用to do。

meanings_zh: n. 吊唁；慰问
definition_en: Sympathy expressed to someone whose relative or friend has died.
example1_en: The seminar spent a few minutes on a message of condolence.
example1_zh: 研讨课花了几分钟讨论慰问信息。
example2_en: In the lecture on social change, everyone remembered the example of a message of condolence.
example2_zh: 在关于社会变迁的讲座里，大家都记得慰问信息这个例子。
collocations: offer condolences｜表示慰问 ; a message of condolence｜慰问信息 ; sincere condolences｜诚挚的哀悼
tip_zh: 常用复数：offer condolences to someone。

meanings_zh: adj. 休眠的；暂不活跃的
definition_en: temporarily inactive but able to become active again
example1_en: The seminar spent a few minutes on dormant volcano.
example1_zh: 研讨课花了几分钟讨论休眠火山。
example2_en: Students compared two sources that both discuss dormant volcano.
example2_zh: 学生比较了两份都讨论休眠火山的材料。
collocations: dormant volcano｜休眠火山 ; lie dormant｜处于休眠状态 ; dormant seeds｜休眠种子 ; dormant account｜长期未使用的账户
tip_zh: 指暂不活动但可能恢复；休眠火山不等于死火山。

meanings_zh: n. 志业；使命感 | n. 职业
definition_en: work you feel strongly suited or called to do | a particular occupation, especially one requiring training
example1_en: Office hours began with a sense of vocation.
example1_zh: 答疑从职业使命感开始。
example2_en: A campus survey used a sense of vocation to explain a pattern in economic policy.
example2_zh: 一项校园调查用职业使命感来解释经济政策中的一种模式。
collocations: find one's vocation｜找到自己的志业 ; a sense of vocation｜职业使命感 ; a vocation for teaching｜从事教学的志向
tip_zh: 常含使命感或天职之意；勿与vacation（假期）混淆。

meanings_zh: v. 使倒置；使颠倒
definition_en: To turn something upside down or reverse its order.
example1_en: I heard the lecturer invert a container during the example.
example1_zh: 我听到讲者在举例时倒置容器。
example2_en: Careful notes from the talk include a reminder to invert a container.
example2_zh: 听课笔记里写着要记得倒置容器。
collocations: invert a container｜倒置容器 ; invert the order｜颠倒顺序 ; invert an image｜翻转图像
tip_zh: 通常是及物动词；倒置的用inverted。

meanings_zh: v. 促使发生；引发 | n. 沉淀物 | adj. 仓促的；鲁莽的
definition_en: To cause something to happen suddenly or sooner than expected. | A solid that forms in a liquid during a chemical reaction. | Done too quickly and without enough thought.
example1_en: The lab instructions say to precipitate a crisis.
example1_zh: 实验说明要求引发危机。
example2_en: A lecture on the natural sciences showed why researchers precipitate a crisis before they publish.
example2_zh: 关于自然科学的讲座说明了研究者为什么在发表之前要引发危机。
collocations: precipitate a crisis｜引发危机 ; precipitate change｜促成变化 ; form a precipitate｜形成沉淀物 ; precipitate action｜仓促的行动
tip_zh: 动词末尾读/teɪt/，名词、形容词读/tət/。

meanings_zh: adj. 怀疑他人动机的；愤世嫉俗的 | adj. 损人利己的；不顾道义的
definition_en: believing people act selfishly rather than honestly or generously | using others selfishly without concern for fairness or honesty
example1_en: The textbook introduces cynical about in the first chapter.
example1_zh: 教材在第一章介绍了对……的动机持怀疑态度。
example2_en: A campus survey used cynical about to explain a pattern in academic research.
example2_zh: 一项校园调查用对……的动机持怀疑态度来解释学术研究中的一种模式。
collocations: cynical about｜对……的动机持怀疑态度 ; a cynical attitude｜愤世嫉俗的态度 ; a cynical attempt｜不顾道义的企图
tip_zh: 常接about，侧重怀疑善意，并非单纯悲观。

meanings_zh: v. 盛行；普遍存在 | v. 获胜；占上风 | v. 说服
definition_en: to be common or widespread in a place or time | to win or become stronger than an opposing force | to persuade someone to do something
example1_en: Before Friday's seminar, our group has to prevail over.
example1_zh: 周五研讨课之前，我们小组必须战胜。
example2_en: Careful notes from the talk include a reminder to prevail over.
example2_zh: 听课笔记里写着要记得战胜。
collocations: prevailing conditions｜普遍状况 ; prevail over｜战胜 ; prevail upon someone to do｜说服某人做
tip_zh: 获胜用prevail over；说服用prevail upon sb to do。

meanings_zh: n. 人类学
definition_en: the study of humans, their societies, cultures, and development
example1_en: Office hours began with cultural anthropology.
example1_zh: 答疑从文化人类学开始。
example2_en: A campus survey used cultural anthropology to explain a pattern in academic research.
example2_zh: 一项校园调查用文化人类学来解释学术研究中的一种模式。
collocations: cultural anthropology｜文化人类学 ; social anthropology｜社会人类学 ; study anthropology｜学习人类学
tip_zh: 通常为不可数名词；研究者称anthropologist。

meanings_zh: n. 润滑
definition_en: The use of oil or similar substances to reduce friction
example1_en: The textbook introduces regular lubrication in the first chapter.
example1_zh: 教材在第一章介绍了定期润滑。
example2_en: The reading connects regular lubrication with a larger point about technological change.
example2_zh: 这篇阅读把定期润滑和关于技术变革的一个更大的问题联系起来。
collocations: regular lubrication｜定期润滑 ; adequate lubrication｜充分润滑 ; lubrication system｜润滑系统 ; lack of lubrication｜缺乏润滑
tip_zh: lubrication指润滑过程；lubricant指润滑剂。

meanings_zh: adj. 顽强的；坚持不懈的
definition_en: Continuing with determination despite difficulties or setbacks.
example1_en: I copied dogged determination into my lecture notes.
example1_zh: 我把顽强的决心抄进了课堂笔记。
example2_en: The listening passage defines the discussion around dogged determination.
example2_zh: 这段听力材料围绕顽强的决心展开说明。
collocations: dogged determination｜顽强的决心 ; dogged persistence｜不懈的坚持 ; dogged pursuit｜执着的追求
tip_zh: 作形容词读两个音节，通常强调不轻言放弃。

meanings_zh: v. 浸没；潜入水中；淹没
definition_en: To go below a liquid's surface or put something there
example1_en: The professor asked us to submerge in water.
example1_zh: 教授让我们浸入水中。
example2_en: When the class discussed environmental policy, the speaker told us to submerge in water.
example2_zh: 全班讨论环境政策时，讲者让我们浸入水中。
collocations: fully submerge｜完全浸没 ; submerge in water｜浸入水中 ; partially submerged｜部分被淹没
tip_zh: 可及物或不及物；强调进入水面或液面以下。

meanings_zh: n. 声望；威望
definition_en: Respect and admiration gained through achievement, quality, or high status.
example1_en: The quiz had a short question about international prestige.
example1_zh: 小测里有一道关于国际声望的简答题。
example2_en: A campus survey used international prestige to explain a pattern in social change.
example2_zh: 一项校园调查用国际声望来解释社会变迁中的一种模式。
collocations: international prestige｜国际声望 ; gain prestige｜获得声望 ; social prestige｜社会声望 ; a matter of prestige｜关乎声望的事
tip_zh: prestige不可数；形容词用prestigious。

meanings_zh: v. 使隶属；加入组织 | n. 附属机构；关联公司
definition_en: To officially connect a person or group with an organisation. | An organisation officially connected with a larger organisation.
example1_en: The professor asked us to affiliate with.
example1_zh: 教授让我们加入；隶属于。
example2_en: In the sample listening, the professor pauses to affiliate with.
example2_zh: 在示例听力里，教授停下来加入；隶属于。
collocations: affiliate with｜加入；隶属于 ; be affiliated with｜与……有隶属关系 ; a local affiliate｜地方附属机构
tip_zh: 名词词尾读 /ət/，动词词尾读 /eɪt/。

meanings_zh: n. 范式；典范
definition_en: A widely accepted model of how a field understands its subject.
example1_en: The seminar called the old textbook a fading paradigm.
example1_zh: 研讨课把那本旧教材称为正在消退的范式。
example2_en: A paradigm shift happens when evidence no longer fits the model everyone uses.
example2_zh: 当证据不再符合人人都在用的模型时，就会发生范式转移。
collocations: paradigm shift｜范式转移 ; a dominant paradigm｜主导范式
tip_zh: 重音在第一音节。学术阅读里常与 shift 搭配。

meanings_zh: n. 问候语；书信称呼语 | n. 致意；致敬
definition_en: Words used to greet someone, especially at a letter's beginning | A gesture or action expressing greeting or respect
example1_en: Our professor circled formal salutation on the slide.
example1_zh: 教授在幻灯片上圈出了正式称呼语。
example2_en: The listening passage defines the discussion around formal salutation.
example2_zh: 这段听力材料围绕正式称呼语展开说明。
collocations: formal salutation｜正式称呼语 ; opening salutation｜开头问候语 ; in salutation｜以示致意
tip_zh: 书信开头的Dear…是salutation；敬礼常用salute。

meanings_zh: adj. 极其细致的；煞费苦心的
definition_en: Done with great care, effort, and attention to detail.
example1_en: Our professor circled painstaking research on the slide.
example1_zh: 教授在幻灯片上圈出了细致深入的研究。
example2_en: A campus survey used painstaking research to explain a pattern in economic policy.
example2_zh: 一项校园调查用细致深入的研究来解释经济政策中的一种模式。
collocations: painstaking research｜细致深入的研究 ; painstaking attention to detail｜对细节的极度关注 ; painstaking work｜精细费力的工作
tip_zh: 是形容词，强调费心且细致，不只是辛苦。

meanings_zh: n. 传教士 | adj. 传教的；传教士的
definition_en: someone sent to teach a religion, often in another country | relating to people or activities that spread a religion
example1_en: The quiz had a short question about missionary work.
example1_zh: 小测里有一道关于传教工作的简答题。
example2_en: In the lecture on historical change, everyone remembered the example of missionary work.
example2_zh: 在关于历史变迁的讲座里，大家都记得传教工作这个例子。
collocations: missionary work｜传教工作 ; a missionary school｜传教学校 ; missionary activity｜传教活动
tip_zh: 可作名词或形容词；复数为missionaries。

meanings_zh: n. 显著；重要；知名
definition_en: The state of being noticeable, important, or widely known.
example1_en: Our professor circled rise to prominence on the slide.
example1_zh: 教授在幻灯片上圈出了崭露头角。
example2_en: The author returns to rise to prominence when explaining the conclusion.
example2_zh: 作者在解释结论时又回到了崭露头角。
collocations: gain prominence｜日益受到关注 ; rise to prominence｜崭露头角 ; give prominence to｜突出；重视
tip_zh: 通常不可数；rise to prominence指崭露头角。

meanings_zh: adj. 明确的；直言的
definition_en: expressed clearly and directly, leaving no doubt about the meaning
example1_en: I copied explicit instructions into my lecture notes.
example1_zh: 我把明确的指示抄进了课堂笔记。
example2_en: The reading connects explicit instructions with a larger point about academic research.
example2_zh: 这篇阅读把明确的指示和关于学术研究的一个更大的问题联系起来。
collocations: explicit instructions｜明确的指示 ; explicit consent｜明确的同意 ; explicit reference｜明确提及 ; make explicit｜明确说明
tip_zh: explicit指明说的；implicit指未明说但可推知的。

meanings_zh: adj. 有限的 | adj. 限定的（动词形式）
definition_en: Having a limit in size, amount, or duration | Having tense and sometimes showing person or number
example1_en: The quiz had a short question about finite resources.
example1_zh: 小测里有一道关于有限的资源的简答题。
example2_en: In the lecture on environmental policy, everyone remembered the example of finite resources.
example2_zh: 在关于环境政策的讲座里，大家都记得有限的资源这个例子。
collocations: finite resources｜有限的资源 ; a finite amount｜有限的数量 ; a finite verb｜限定动词
tip_zh: 读音重音在首音节；勿按finish的元音读。

meanings_zh: n. 夹具；夹钳 | v. 夹紧；固定
definition_en: A device that holds objects tightly together or in place. | To hold something firmly, often using a gripping device.
example1_en: Office hours began with a metal clamp.
example1_zh: 答疑从金属夹具开始。
example2_en: Students compared two sources that both discuss a metal clamp.
example2_zh: 学生比较了两份都讨论金属夹具的材料。
collocations: a metal clamp｜金属夹具 ; clamp something in place｜将某物夹紧固定 ; clamp down on｜严厉打击；严格限制
tip_zh: clamp down on是短语动词，指严厉打击或限制。

meanings_zh: n. 配额；限额
definition_en: an officially fixed amount allowed, required, or assigned
example1_en: I copied an import quota into my lecture notes.
example1_zh: 我把进口配额抄进了课堂笔记。
example2_en: In the lecture on economic policy, everyone remembered the example of an import quota.
example2_zh: 在关于经济政策的讲座里，大家都记得进口配额这个例子。
collocations: an import quota｜进口配额 ; a fishing quota｜捕捞配额 ; meet a quota｜完成配额指标 ; impose a quota｜设定配额
tip_zh: 既可指允许的上限，也可指必须完成的指标。

meanings_zh: v. 激起；引起 | v. 唤醒
definition_en: To cause a feeling, interest, or reaction. | To wake someone from sleep.
example1_en: I heard the lecturer arouse curiosity during the example.
example1_zh: 我听到讲者在举例时激起好奇心。
example2_en: The reading asks you to arouse curiosity and then check a second source.
example2_zh: 这篇阅读要求你激起好奇心，然后再核对第二个来源。
collocations: arouse curiosity｜激起好奇心 ; arouse suspicion｜引起怀疑 ; arouse interest｜引起兴趣 ; arouse opposition｜激起反对
tip_zh: arouse 后接宾语；arise 表示“出现”，不接宾语。

meanings_zh: n. 赞助人；资助者 | n. 顾客；常客
definition_en: Someone who supports an artist, organisation, or activity, often financially. | A customer of a restaurant, theatre, or similar place.
example1_en: The quiz had a short question about wealthy patron.
example1_zh: 小测里有一道关于富有的资助者的简答题。
example2_en: Students compared two sources that both discuss wealthy patron.
example2_zh: 学生比较了两份都讨论富有的资助者的材料。
collocations: patron of the arts｜艺术赞助人 ; wealthy patron｜富有的资助者 ; regular patron｜常客
tip_zh: patron既指资助者，也可正式地指餐馆等的顾客。

meanings_zh: adj. 有偿债能力的 | n. 溶剂
definition_en: Able to pay all the money that is owed. | A substance, usually liquid, that dissolves another substance.
example1_en: Office hours began with an organic solvent.
example1_zh: 答疑从有机溶剂开始。
example2_en: The author returns to an organic solvent when explaining the conclusion.
example2_zh: 作者在解释结论时又回到了有机溶剂。
collocations: remain solvent｜保持偿债能力 ; a solvent company｜有偿债能力的公司 ; an organic solvent｜有机溶剂 ; a powerful solvent｜强效溶剂
tip_zh: 形容词指能偿债，不等于盈利；名词指溶剂。

meanings_zh: n. 肿瘤
definition_en: an abnormal mass of cells growing in the body
example1_en: The seminar spent a few minutes on benign tumour.
example1_zh: 研讨课花了几分钟讨论良性肿瘤。
example2_en: The author returns to benign tumour when explaining the conclusion.
example2_zh: 作者在解释结论时又回到了良性肿瘤。
collocations: benign tumour｜良性肿瘤 ; malignant tumour｜恶性肿瘤 ; remove a tumour｜切除肿瘤 ; tumour growth｜肿瘤生长
tip_zh: 英式拼写tumour，美式tumor；肿瘤不一定是癌。

meanings_zh: n. 先知 | n. 预言者
definition_en: Someone believed to communicate messages from a god. | Someone who predicts future events or developments.
example1_en: Office hours began with a religious prophet.
example1_zh: 答疑从宗教先知开始。
example2_en: The author returns to a religious prophet when explaining the conclusion.
example2_zh: 作者在解释结论时又回到了宗教先知。
collocations: a religious prophet｜宗教先知 ; a prophet of doom｜灾难预言者 ; the teachings of a prophet｜先知的教诲
tip_zh: 与profit（利润）同音；动词为prophesy。

meanings_zh: v. 违反；违背 | v. 侵犯；侵害
definition_en: To act against a law, rule, or agreement. | To fail to respect someone's rights or privacy.
example1_en: In office hours we practiced how to violate the law.
example1_zh: 答疑时我们练习如何违法。
example2_en: Careful notes from the talk include a reminder to violate the law.
example2_zh: 听课笔记里写着要记得违法。
collocations: violate the law｜违法 ; violate an agreement｜违反协议 ; violate human rights｜侵犯人权 ; violate someone's privacy｜侵犯某人的隐私
tip_zh: 及物动词，直接接法律、协议、权利等宾语。

meanings_zh: v. 耕作；栽培 | v. 培养；发展
definition_en: To prepare land for crops or grow plants | To deliberately develop a skill, quality, interest, or relationship
example1_en: The professor asked us to cultivate crops.
example1_zh: 教授让我们种植作物。
example2_en: The reading asks you to cultivate crops and then check a second source.
example2_zh: 这篇阅读要求你种植作物，然后再核对第二个来源。
collocations: cultivate crops｜种植作物 ; cultivate the land｜耕种土地 ; cultivate an interest in｜培养对……的兴趣 ; cultivate relationships｜经营关系
tip_zh: 既可指种植作物，也可指有意识地培养兴趣或关系。

meanings_zh: n. 详细阐述；补充说明
definition_en: The addition of details to explain or develop something.
example1_en: The quiz had a short question about further elaboration.
example1_zh: 小测里有一道关于进一步阐述的简答题。
example2_en: The reading connects further elaboration with a larger point about academic research.
example2_zh: 这篇阅读把进一步阐述和关于学术研究的一个更大的问题联系起来。
collocations: further elaboration｜进一步阐述 ; elaboration on a point｜对某一点的详细说明 ; without elaboration｜未作详细说明
tip_zh: 说明某一点常用elaboration on；动词为elaborate。

meanings_zh: n. 告示牌；标语牌
definition_en: a large notice displayed publicly or carried during a demonstration
example1_en: I copied protest placard into my lecture notes.
example1_zh: 我把抗议标语牌抄进了课堂笔记。
example2_en: The author returns to protest placard when explaining the conclusion.
example2_zh: 作者在解释结论时又回到了抗议标语牌。
collocations: carry a placard｜举着标语牌 ; hold up a placard｜举起标语牌 ; protest placard｜抗议标语牌
tip_zh: 通常指公开展示或游行时举着的大幅告示牌。

meanings_zh: n. 怀旧；对往昔的眷恋
definition_en: warm, sometimes sad feelings about happy times in the past
example1_en: The seminar spent a few minutes on a wave of nostalgia.
example1_zh: 研讨课花了几分钟讨论一阵怀旧之情。
example2_en: In the lecture on human behavior, everyone remembered the example of a wave of nostalgia.
example2_zh: 在关于人类行为的讲座里，大家都记得一阵怀旧之情这个例子。
collocations: nostalgia for the past｜对往昔的眷恋 ; a wave of nostalgia｜一阵怀旧之情 ; evoke nostalgia｜唤起怀旧之情
tip_zh: 通常不可数；nostalgia for后接怀念的时期或事物。

meanings_zh: n. 对手；敌对者 | n. 故事中的对立角色
definition_en: Someone who strongly opposes another person. | A character who opposes the main character in a story.
example1_en: The quiz had a short question about a formidable antagonist.
example1_zh: 小测里有一道关于强大的对手的简答题。
example2_en: The author returns to a formidable antagonist when explaining the conclusion.
example2_zh: 作者在解释结论时又回到了强大的对手。
collocations: a formidable antagonist｜强大的对手 ; the main antagonist｜主要对立角色 ; a political antagonist｜政敌
tip_zh: 故事中的antagonist与主角对立，不一定是坏人。

meanings_zh: v. 使失去法律效力 | v. 抵消；使无效
definition_en: to make an agreement or decision legally invalid | to remove the effect or value of something
example1_en: The assignment is to nullify a contract, then say why it matters.
example1_zh: 作业是先使合同无效，再说明它为什么重要。
example2_en: The passage says students who can nullify a contract follow the argument more easily.
example2_zh: 文章说，能够使合同无效的学生更容易跟上论点。
collocations: nullify a contract｜使合同无效 ; nullify a decision｜使决定失效 ; nullify the benefits｜抵消益处
tip_zh: 既可指法律上作废，也可指效果被抵消。

meanings_zh: n. 解剖学 | n. 身体构造
definition_en: the scientific study of the structure of living bodies | the physical structure of a human, animal, or plant
example1_en: Office hours began with human anatomy.
example1_zh: 答疑从人体解剖学开始。
example2_en: In the lecture on the natural sciences, everyone remembered the example of human anatomy.
example2_zh: 在关于自然科学的讲座里，大家都记得人体解剖学这个例子。
collocations: human anatomy｜人体解剖学 ; study anatomy｜学习解剖学 ; comparative anatomy｜比较解剖学
tip_zh: anatomy侧重身体结构，physiology侧重生理功能。

meanings_zh: adv. 彻底地；直截了当地 | adv. 一次付清地；完全拥有地 | adj. 完全的；公然的
definition_en: Completely, immediately, or without hiding what you mean. | With full payment or ownership, rather than borrowing or sharing. | Complete or clear, with no attempt to hide it.
example1_en: The professor explained outright with a short example from campus.
example1_zh: 教授用一个简短的校园例子解释了彻底地。
example2_en: A reading on social change uses outright when the author sets up the main claim.
example2_zh: 一篇关于社会变迁的阅读在提出主要主张时用到了彻底地。
collocations: reject outright｜断然拒绝 ; buy outright｜一次付清购买 ; an outright ban｜全面禁令 ; an outright lie｜彻头彻尾的谎言
tip_zh: buy outright指一次付清；形容词常置于名词前。

meanings_zh: adj. 难以想象的；不可接受的
definition_en: too unlikely or unacceptable to imagine or consider seriously
example1_en: The quiz had a short question about previously unthinkable.
example1_zh: 小测里有一道关于以前难以想象的的简答题。
example2_en: A campus survey used previously unthinkable to explain a pattern in academic research.
example2_zh: 一项校园调查用以前难以想象的来解释学术研究中的一种模式。
collocations: an unthinkable idea｜不可接受的想法 ; previously unthinkable｜以前难以想象的 ; unthinkable consequences｜难以想象的后果
tip_zh: 比unlikely语气更强，常含“根本不能接受”之意。

meanings_zh: v. 擅自进入；非法侵入 | n. 擅自进入；非法侵入行为
definition_en: to enter someone's land or property without permission | the act of entering someone's property without permission
example1_en: In office hours we practiced how to trespass on private property.
example1_zh: 答疑时我们练习如何擅闯私人地产。
example2_en: A lecture on social change showed why researchers trespass on private property before they publish.
example2_zh: 关于社会变迁的讲座说明了研究者为什么在发表之前要擅闯私人地产。
collocations: trespass on private property｜擅闯私人地产 ; trespass on someone's land｜擅自进入他人的土地
tip_zh: 表示擅闯某地常用trespass on，不指一般过失。

meanings_zh: adj. 可行的；能成功的 | adj. 能存活的；能发育的
definition_en: Able to work successfully in practice. | Able to survive or develop into a living organism.
example1_en: The quiz had a short question about economically viable.
example1_zh: 小测里有一道关于经济上可行的的简答题。
example2_en: A campus survey used economically viable to explain a pattern in academic research.
example2_zh: 一项校园调查用经济上可行的来解释学术研究中的一种模式。
collocations: viable option｜可行的选择 ; economically viable｜经济上可行的 ; viable solution｜可行的解决方案 ; viable seeds｜有发芽能力的种子
tip_zh: 主要指方案可行；生物学中指能存活或发育。

meanings_zh: adj. 临时的；过渡期间的 | n. 过渡期间；间隔时期
definition_en: Intended to last until a permanent arrangement is made. | The period before a later event or permanent arrangement.
example1_en: The quiz had a short question about interim report.
example1_zh: 小测里有一道关于阶段性报告的简答题。
example2_en: A campus survey used interim report to explain a pattern in economic policy.
example2_zh: 一项校园调查用阶段性报告来解释经济政策中的一种模式。
collocations: interim report｜阶段性报告 ; interim measures｜临时措施 ; interim manager｜临时经理 ; in the interim｜在此期间
tip_zh: 形容词常置于名词前；in the interim意为在此期间。

meanings_zh: n. 繁殖；育种 | n. 教养
definition_en: Animal reproduction, or controlled reproduction of animals and plants. | Polite behaviour learned through someone's upbringing.
example1_en: The quiz had a short question about selective breeding.
example1_zh: 小测里有一道关于选择性育种的简答题。
example2_en: The reading connects selective breeding with a larger point about the natural sciences.
example2_zh: 这篇阅读把选择性育种和关于自然科学的一个更大的问题联系起来。
collocations: breeding season｜繁殖季节 ; selective breeding｜选择性育种 ; captive breeding｜圈养繁殖 ; breeding programme｜繁育计划
tip_zh: breeding侧重繁殖或人工育种；breed作名词指品种。

meanings_zh: adj. 贫瘠的；不毛的 | adj. 无成果的；缺乏的
definition_en: Unable to support much plant growth. | Producing nothing useful or lacking something important.
example1_en: The seminar spent a few minutes on barren land.
example1_zh: 研讨课花了几分钟讨论荒地。
example2_en: The reading connects barren land with a larger point about environmental policy.
example2_zh: 这篇阅读把荒地和关于环境政策的一个更大的问题联系起来。
collocations: barren land｜荒地 ; barren landscape｜荒芜的景观 ; barren of｜缺乏……的
tip_zh: barren强调不生长或无产出；bare强调裸露、无遮挡。

meanings_zh: n. 袭击；侵犯人身 | v. 袭击；殴打
definition_en: a violent physical attack on someone | to attack someone physically
example1_en: Office hours began with physical assault.
example1_zh: 答疑从人身攻击开始。
example2_en: The listening passage defines the discussion around physical assault.
example2_zh: 这段听力材料围绕人身攻击展开说明。
collocations: physical assault｜人身攻击 ; an assault on someone｜对某人的袭击 ; report an assault｜报告袭击事件
tip_zh: 名词常接on；动词直接接人，不加介词。

meanings_zh: v. 使有活力；使生动 | v. 把…制作成动画
definition_en: To make someone or something more lively or engaging | To make drawings or models appear to move
example1_en: I heard the lecturer animate a discussion during the example.
example1_zh: 我听到讲者在举例时使讨论活跃。
example2_en: In the sample listening, the professor pauses to animate a discussion.
example2_zh: 在示例听力里，教授停下来使讨论活跃。
collocations: animate a discussion｜使讨论活跃 ; animate a character｜把角色制作成动画 ; animated film｜动画电影
tip_zh: 动词末尾读/meɪt/；形容词末尾读/mət/。

meanings_zh: adj. 暂定的；初步的 | adj. 犹豫的；试探性的
definition_en: Not yet definite and possibly subject to change. | Showing uncertainty or a lack of confidence.
example1_en: Office hours began with tentative plans.
example1_zh: 答疑从暂定计划开始。
example2_en: The reading connects tentative plans with a larger point about academic research.
example2_zh: 这篇阅读把暂定计划和关于学术研究的一个更大的问题联系起来。
collocations: tentative plans｜暂定计划 ; a tentative conclusion｜初步结论 ; a tentative agreement｜初步协议 ; a tentative smile｜试探性的微笑
tip_zh: 既可指计划“暂定”，也可指动作“试探性”。

meanings_zh: adj. 按时间顺序的
definition_en: Arranged in the order in which events happened.
example1_en: Office hours began with chronological order.
example1_zh: 答疑从时间顺序开始。
example2_en: The listening passage defines the discussion around chronological order.
example2_zh: 这段听力材料围绕时间顺序展开说明。
collocations: chronological order｜时间顺序 ; chronological account｜按时间顺序的叙述 ; chronological sequence｜时间先后次序
tip_zh: 强调事件发生的先后，不是重要性或逻辑顺序。

meanings_zh: v. 深入调查；探查 | n. 深入调查 | n. 探针；探测器
definition_en: To examine something closely to discover hidden information. | A detailed investigation into a problem or suspected wrongdoing. | An instrument or spacecraft used to examine or explore something.
example1_en: I heard the lecturer probe into during the example.
example1_zh: 我听到讲者在举例时深入调查。
example2_en: When the class discussed the natural sciences, the speaker told us to probe into.
example2_zh: 全班讨论自然科学时，讲者让我们深入调查。
collocations: probe into｜深入调查 ; launch a probe｜启动调查 ; space probe｜太空探测器 ; a medical probe｜医用探针
tip_zh: 动词可直接接调查对象，也可用probe into。

meanings_zh: n. 细微差别
definition_en: a small difference in meaning, feeling, sound, or appearance
example1_en: The seminar spent a few minutes on subtle nuance.
example1_zh: 研讨课花了几分钟讨论微妙差别。
example2_en: Students compared two sources that both discuss subtle nuance.
example2_zh: 学生比较了两份都讨论微妙差别的材料。
collocations: subtle nuance｜微妙差别 ; nuances of meaning｜意义上的细微差别 ; capture the nuances｜捕捉细微差别
tip_zh: 常用复数nuances，指意义、语气等细微差别。

meanings_zh: n. 走私；非法偷运
definition_en: Illegally moving goods or people across borders or past controls.
example1_en: The textbook introduces wildlife smuggling in the first chapter.
example1_zh: 教材在第一章介绍了野生动物走私。
example2_en: Students compared two sources that both discuss wildlife smuggling.
example2_zh: 学生比较了两份都讨论野生动物走私的材料。
collocations: wildlife smuggling｜野生动物走私 ; a smuggling ring｜走私团伙 ; combat smuggling｜打击走私
tip_zh: 通常不可数；动词搭配smuggle goods into a country。

meanings_zh: adj. 成比例的 | adj. 相称的；适度的
definition_en: changing in a constant ratio to another quantity | appropriate in size or degree compared with something else
example1_en: The seminar spent a few minutes on directly proportional to.
example1_zh: 研讨课花了几分钟讨论与……成正比。
example2_en: The reading connects directly proportional to with a larger point about the natural sciences.
example2_zh: 这篇阅读把与……成正比和关于自然科学的一个更大的问题联系起来。
collocations: directly proportional to｜与……成正比 ; inversely proportional to｜与……成反比 ; proportional representation｜比例代表制
tip_zh: 常与to搭配；成正比用directly proportional to。

meanings_zh: n. 受尊敬的资深政治家
definition_en: an experienced male political leader respected for wisdom and judgement
example1_en: The seminar spent a few minutes on elder statesman.
example1_zh: 研讨课花了几分钟讨论政坛元老。
example2_en: The listening passage defines the discussion around elder statesman.
example2_zh: 这段听力材料围绕政坛元老展开说明。
collocations: elder statesman｜政坛元老 ; respected statesman｜受尊敬的政治家 ; distinguished statesman｜杰出的政治家
tip_zh: 通常含褒义，不宜译作贬义的“政客”；女性用 stateswoman。

meanings_zh: v. 制定；通过法律 | v. 表演；演出
definition_en: To make a proposal officially become law. | To perform a story or event through acting.
example1_en: In office hours we practiced how to enact legislation.
example1_zh: 答疑时我们练习如何制定法律。
example2_en: In the sample listening, the professor pauses to enact legislation.
example2_zh: 在示例听力里，教授停下来制定法律。
collocations: enact legislation｜制定法律 ; enact a law｜通过一项法律 ; enact a scene｜表演一个场景
tip_zh: enact指制定或通过法律；enforce指执行法律。

meanings_zh: adj. 双性恋的
definition_en: bisexual; romantically or sexually attracted to more than one gender
example1_en: Our professor circled openly bi on the slide.
example1_zh: 教授在幻灯片上圈出了公开双性恋身份的。
example2_en: Students compared two sources that both discuss openly bi.
example2_zh: 学生比较了两份都讨论公开双性恋身份的的材料。
collocations: bi people｜双性恋者 ; bi identity｜双性恋身份认同 ; openly bi｜公开双性恋身份的
tip_zh: bi是bisexual的非正式简称；勿与前缀bi-混淆。

meanings_zh: adj. 审美的；美学的
definition_en: Relating to beauty or the appreciation of beautiful things.
example1_en: The quiz had a short question about esthetic appeal.
example1_zh: 小测里有一道关于审美吸引力的简答题。
example2_en: The author returns to esthetic appeal when explaining the conclusion.
example2_zh: 作者在解释结论时又回到了审美吸引力。
collocations: esthetic appeal｜审美吸引力 ; esthetic value｜美学价值 ; esthetic qualities｜美感特质
tip_zh: esthetic 是美式拼写，英式多为 aesthetic。托福写作用美式即可。

meanings_zh: adj. 无机的
definition_en: relating to substances generally without carbon bonded to hydrogen
example1_en: Office hours began with inorganic chemistry.
example1_zh: 答疑从无机化学开始。
example2_en: In the lecture on the natural sciences, everyone remembered the example of inorganic chemistry.
example2_zh: 在关于自然科学的讲座里，大家都记得无机化学这个例子。
collocations: inorganic chemistry｜无机化学 ; inorganic compounds｜无机化合物 ; inorganic fertilisers｜无机肥料 ; inorganic matter｜无机物
tip_zh: 无机物并非都不含碳，如二氧化碳也是无机物。

meanings_zh: n. 荒漠化；沙漠化
definition_en: the process by which productive land becomes desert
example1_en: I copied combat desertification into my lecture notes.
example1_zh: 我把防治荒漠化抄进了课堂笔记。
example2_en: A campus survey used combat desertification to explain a pattern in environmental policy.
example2_zh: 一项校园调查用防治荒漠化来解释环境政策中的一种模式。
collocations: combat desertification｜防治荒漠化 ; prevent desertification｜防止荒漠化 ; land degradation and desertification｜土地退化与荒漠化
tip_zh: 不可数名词；强调土地逐渐退化为荒漠。

meanings_zh: v. 开始从事；着手 | v. 上船；登机
definition_en: To begin a project, activity, or course of action | To board a ship or aircraft for a journey
example1_en: I heard the lecturer embark on a project during the example.
example1_zh: 我听到讲者在举例时着手开展项目。
example2_en: Careful notes from the talk include a reminder to embark on a project.
example2_zh: 听课笔记里写着要记得着手开展项目。
collocations: embark on a project｜着手开展项目 ; embark on a career｜开始职业生涯 ; embark on a journey｜踏上旅程
tip_zh: 表示着手做某事时，用embark on或upon。

meanings_zh: n. 凝聚力；团结 | n. 篇章衔接
definition_en: The strength of connection that keeps a group together | The way parts of a text connect through language
example1_en: The quiz had a short question about social cohesion.
example1_zh: 小测里有一道关于社会凝聚力的简答题。
example2_en: The reading connects social cohesion with a larger point about social change.
example2_zh: 这篇阅读把社会凝聚力和关于社会变迁的一个更大的问题联系起来。
collocations: social cohesion｜社会凝聚力 ; team cohesion｜团队凝聚力 ; cohesion and coherence｜衔接与连贯
tip_zh: 写作中cohesion指语言衔接，coherence指逻辑连贯。

meanings_zh: n. 征服；攻占 | n. 征服的领土
definition_en: the act of taking control of a country by force | a place brought under control through military force
example1_en: I copied military conquest into my lecture notes.
example1_zh: 我把军事征服抄进了课堂笔记。
example2_en: Students compared two sources that both discuss military conquest.
example2_zh: 学生比较了两份都讨论军事征服的材料。
collocations: military conquest｜军事征服 ; territorial conquest｜领土征服 ; wars of conquest｜征服战争
tip_zh: 表示征服行为可不可数；指征服的领土时可数。

meanings_zh: n. 竞争；对抗
definition_en: Competition between people or groups seeking the same success.
example1_en: Our professor circled intense rivalry on the slide.
example1_zh: 教授在幻灯片上圈出了激烈竞争。
example2_en: In the lecture on social change, everyone remembered the example of intense rivalry.
example2_zh: 在关于社会变迁的讲座里，大家都记得激烈竞争这个例子。
collocations: intense rivalry｜激烈竞争 ; sibling rivalry｜兄弟姐妹间的竞争 ; rivalry between teams｜队伍之间的竞争
tip_zh: 强调持续的竞争关系，双方之间常用between。

meanings_zh: v. 使发懵；使恍惚 | n. 恍惚；迷茫状态
definition_en: To leave someone confused and unable to think clearly. | A state of confusion or reduced awareness.
example1_en: The professor explained daze with a short example from campus.
example1_zh: 教授用一个简短的校园例子解释了使发懵。
example2_en: A reading on academic research uses daze when the author sets up the main claim.
example2_zh: 一篇关于学术研究的阅读在提出主要主张时用到了使发懵。
collocations: in a daze｜处于恍惚状态 ; leave someone dazed｜使某人发懵 ; look dazed｜显得茫然
tip_zh: in a daze指恍惚；表示光线刺眼通常用dazzle。

meanings_zh: n. 评判标准；准则
definition_en: A standard used to judge something or make a decision.
example1_en: After the lecture, we used criterion in a sentence of our own.
example1_zh: 讲座之后，我们在自己的句子里用了准则。
example2_en: A reading on academic research uses criterion when the author sets up the main claim.
example2_zh: 一篇关于学术研究的阅读在提出主要主张时用到了准则。
collocations: meet a criterion｜符合一项标准 ; selection criteria｜筛选标准 ; assessment criteria｜评估标准
tip_zh: 单数criterion，复数criteria；不能说a criteria。

meanings_zh: adj. 人道主义的 | n. 人道主义者
definition_en: Concerned with reducing suffering and improving people's lives. | Someone who works to reduce suffering and improve human welfare.
example1_en: Office hours began with humanitarian aid.
example1_zh: 答疑从人道主义援助开始。
example2_en: The author returns to humanitarian aid when explaining the conclusion.
example2_zh: 作者在解释结论时又回到了人道主义援助。
collocations: humanitarian aid｜人道主义援助 ; humanitarian crisis｜人道主义危机 ; humanitarian grounds｜人道主义理由
tip_zh: 强调减轻人类苦难，不等同于一般的慷慨。

meanings_zh: n. 郑重承诺；誓言 | v. 郑重承诺；保证
definition_en: A serious promise to do or provide something | Formally promise to do or give something
example1_en: The textbook introduces pledge support in the first chapter.
example1_zh: 教材在第一章介绍了承诺支持。
example2_en: The author returns to pledge support when explaining the conclusion.
example2_zh: 作者在解释结论时又回到了承诺支持。
collocations: make a pledge｜作出承诺 ; honour a pledge｜履行承诺 ; pledge support｜承诺支持 ; pledge to do something｜承诺做某事
tip_zh: 比promise更正式；动词常接to do。

meanings_zh: adj. 显眼的；引人注目的
definition_en: easy to notice because of being unusual or different
example1_en: The textbook introduces conspicuous consumption in the first chapter.
example1_zh: 教材在第一章介绍了炫耀性消费。
example2_en: Students compared two sources that both discuss conspicuous consumption.
example2_zh: 学生比较了两份都讨论炫耀性消费的材料。
collocations: conspicuous consumption｜炫耀性消费 ; a conspicuous place｜显眼的位置 ; conspicuous by its absence｜因缺失而格外引人注意
tip_zh: 强调容易被注意到，不一定表示重要。

meanings_zh: n. 火药；黑火药
definition_en: An explosive powder historically used in guns and still in fireworks.
example1_en: Our professor circled the invention of gunpowder on the slide.
example1_zh: 教授在幻灯片上圈出了火药的发明。
example2_en: A campus survey used the invention of gunpowder to explain a pattern in historical change.
example2_zh: 一项校园调查用火药的发明来解释历史变迁中的一种模式。
collocations: the invention of gunpowder｜火药的发明 ; a barrel of gunpowder｜一桶火药 ; gunpowder storage｜火药储存
tip_zh: 不可数名词；一桶火药用a barrel of gunpowder。

meanings_zh: v. 抢救；打捞 | v. 挽救；挽回 | n. 抢救；打捞；获救财物
definition_en: To save useful things from damage, loss, or destruction. | To prevent a situation or effort from failing completely. | The recovery of damaged property, or the property recovered.
example1_en: I heard the lecturer salvage materials during the example.
example1_zh: 我听到讲者在举例时抢救回收材料。
example2_en: The reading asks you to salvage materials and then check a second source.
example2_zh: 这篇阅读要求你抢救回收材料，然后再核对第二个来源。
collocations: salvage materials｜抢救回收材料 ; salvage operation｜抢救作业 ; salvage a reputation｜挽回声誉
tip_zh: 多指抢救财物；救人通常用rescue。

meanings_zh: v. 劫持交通工具 | v. 操控；劫用
definition_en: to illegally seize control of a vehicle during a journey | to take control of something for your own purposes
example1_en: The lab instructions say to hijack a plane.
example1_zh: 实验说明要求劫持飞机。
example2_en: In the sample listening, the professor pauses to hijack a plane.
example2_zh: 在示例听力里，教授停下来劫持飞机。
collocations: hijack a plane｜劫持飞机 ; hijack a debate｜操控讨论 ; hijack the conversation｜把谈话据为己用
tip_zh: 本义是劫持交通工具；也可比喻操控讨论或议程。

meanings_zh: n. 期刊；杂志 | adj. 定期的；周期性的
definition_en: A publication released regularly, containing articles on particular subjects. | Happening or appearing repeatedly at intervals.
example1_en: Our professor circled academic periodical on the slide.
example1_zh: 教授在幻灯片上圈出了学术期刊。
example2_en: The author returns to academic periodical when explaining the conclusion.
example2_zh: 作者在解释结论时又回到了学术期刊。
collocations: academic periodical｜学术期刊 ; monthly periodical｜月刊 ; periodical publication｜定期出版物
tip_zh: 名词指期刊；表示定期发生时，periodic更常用。

meanings_zh: n. 陆军或空军上校
definition_en: a senior army or air force officer
example1_en: The seminar spent a few minutes on an army colonel.
example1_zh: 研讨课花了几分钟讨论陆军上校。
example2_en: A campus survey used an army colonel to explain a pattern in public institutions.
example2_zh: 一项校园调查用陆军上校来解释公共制度中的一种模式。
collocations: an army colonel｜陆军上校 ; promoted to colonel｜晋升为上校 ; a retired colonel｜退役上校
tip_zh: 发音与kernel相同，字母l在此不发/l/音。

meanings_zh: n. 玻璃纤维；玻璃钢
definition_en: fine glass fibres, or plastic strengthened with these fibres
example1_en: The quiz had a short question about fibreglass insulation.
example1_zh: 小测里有一道关于玻璃纤维隔热材料的简答题。
example2_en: The reading connects fibreglass insulation with a larger point about technological change.
example2_zh: 这篇阅读把玻璃纤维隔热材料和关于技术变革的一个更大的问题联系起来。
collocations: fibreglass insulation｜玻璃纤维隔热材料 ; a fibreglass boat｜玻璃钢船 ; fibreglass panels｜玻璃钢板
tip_zh: 英式拼写fibreglass，美式拼写fiberglass。

meanings_zh: n. 动脉 | n. 交通干道；要道
definition_en: A blood vessel carrying blood away from the heart. | A main road or route carrying heavy traffic.
example1_en: The seminar spent a few minutes on coronary artery.
example1_zh: 研讨课花了几分钟讨论冠状动脉。
example2_en: A campus survey used coronary artery to explain a pattern in public health.
example2_zh: 一项校园调查用冠状动脉来解释公共卫生中的一种模式。
collocations: coronary artery｜冠状动脉 ; blocked artery｜堵塞的动脉 ; major artery｜交通要道
tip_zh: 动脉将血液送离心脏；静脉是vein。

meanings_zh: n. 蹄
definition_en: the hard covering of a horse's or similar animal's foot
example1_en: I copied a horse's hoof into my lecture notes.
example1_zh: 我把马蹄抄进了课堂笔记。
example2_en: The author returns to a horse's hoof when explaining the conclusion.
example2_zh: 作者在解释结论时又回到了马蹄。
collocations: hoof care｜蹄部护理 ; hoof print｜蹄印 ; a horse's hoof｜马蹄
tip_zh: 复数hooves和hoofs都正确，hooves更常见。

meanings_zh: n. 监狱 | v. 监禁
definition_en: An older British spelling of jail, a place holding prisoners. | To put someone in prison; an older spelling of jail.
example1_en: Our professor circled old gaol on the slide.
example1_zh: 教授在幻灯片上圈出了旧监狱。
example2_en: In the lecture on historical change, everyone remembered the example of old gaol.
example2_zh: 在关于历史变迁的讲座里，大家都记得旧监狱这个例子。
collocations: old gaol｜旧监狱 ; gaol sentence｜监禁刑罚 ; gaol cell｜牢房
tip_zh: gaol是jail的旧式英式拼法，读音相同。

meanings_zh: adj. 前所未有的；空前的
definition_en: Never having happened or existed before.
example1_en: Office hours began with unprecedented growth.
example1_zh: 答疑从空前的增长开始。
example2_en: Students compared two sources that both discuss unprecedented growth.
example2_zh: 学生比较了两份都讨论空前的增长的材料。
collocations: unprecedented growth｜空前的增长 ; on an unprecedented scale｜以空前的规模 ; unprecedented challenges｜前所未有的挑战
tip_zh: 强调从未发生过，不只是程度很大或不常见。

meanings_zh: n. 青少年违法行为 | n. 逾期未付款
definition_en: illegal or unacceptable behaviour, especially by young people | failure to make a required payment on time
example1_en: The textbook introduces juvenile delinquency in the first chapter.
example1_zh: 教材在第一章介绍了青少年违法犯罪。
example2_en: In the lecture on social change, everyone remembered the example of juvenile delinquency.
example2_zh: 在关于社会变迁的讲座里，大家都记得青少年违法犯罪这个例子。
collocations: juvenile delinquency｜青少年违法犯罪 ; prevent delinquency｜预防违法行为 ; loan delinquency｜贷款逾期
tip_zh: 常见于juvenile delinquency，不能泛指普通小错误。

meanings_zh: adj. 法医的；司法鉴定的 | adj. 细致严密的
definition_en: relating to scientific methods used to investigate crime | examining details with great care and precision
example1_en: The quiz had a short question about forensic science.
example1_zh: 小测里有一道关于司法鉴定科学的简答题。
example2_en: In the lecture on the natural sciences, everyone remembered the example of forensic science.
example2_zh: 在关于自然科学的讲座里，大家都记得司法鉴定科学这个例子。
collocations: forensic science｜司法鉴定科学 ; forensic evidence｜科学鉴定证据 ; forensic analysis｜司法鉴定分析 ; forensic examination｜法医检验；细致审查
tip_zh: forensic通常作形容词；学科名词常用forensics。

meanings_zh: n. 动物的须 | n. 胡须；络腮胡子
definition_en: a long, stiff hair growing near an animal's mouth | a hair growing on a man's cheeks or chin
example1_en: The professor explained whisker with a short example from campus.
example1_zh: 教授用一个简短的校园例子解释了动物的须。
example2_en: Students who can explain whisker usually follow the rest of a lecture on the natural sciences.
example2_zh: 能解释动物的须的学生，通常跟得上一节关于自然科学的讲座。
collocations: a cat's whiskers｜猫的胡须 ; twitch its whiskers｜抖动胡须 ; by a whisker｜以微弱差距
tip_zh: 通常用复数whiskers；by a whisker表示仅差一点。

meanings_zh: adj. 认知的
definition_en: Related to mental processes such as learning, remembering, and understanding.
example1_en: The seminar spent a few minutes on cognitive development.
example1_zh: 研讨课花了几分钟讨论认知发展。
example2_en: A campus survey used cognitive development to explain a pattern in human behavior.
example2_zh: 一项校园调查用认知发展来解释人类行为中的一种模式。
collocations: cognitive development｜认知发展 ; cognitive ability｜认知能力 ; cognitive decline｜认知衰退 ; cognitive function｜认知功能
tip_zh: 常修饰ability、development等，侧重思维和记忆。

meanings_zh: v. 屠宰；宰杀 | n. 屠宰；大规模杀戮 | v. 屠杀
definition_en: To kill animals, usually for food | The killing of animals for food, or many people cruelly | To kill many people cruelly, especially those unable to defend themselves
example1_en: In office hours we practiced how to slaughter animals.
example1_zh: 答疑时我们练习如何屠宰动物。
example2_en: In the sample listening, the professor pauses to slaughter animals.
example2_zh: 在示例听力里，教授停下来屠宰动物。
collocations: slaughter animals｜屠宰动物 ; slaughter for food｜宰杀供食用 ; mass slaughter｜大规模屠杀
tip_zh: 指宰杀动物或残酷杀戮，语气强；不用于普通死亡。

meanings_zh: v. 增强；加剧；使强化
definition_en: become stronger or more extreme, or make something so
example1_en: I heard the lecturer intensify efforts during the example.
example1_zh: 我听到讲者在举例时加大力度。
example2_en: A lecture on environmental policy showed why researchers intensify efforts before they publish.
example2_zh: 关于环境政策的讲座说明了研究者为什么在发表之前要加大力度。
collocations: intensify efforts｜加大力度 ; intensify pressure｜加大压力 ; competition intensifies｜竞争加剧
tip_zh: 可直接接宾语，也可不接：压力本身也会加剧。

meanings_zh: adj. 杰出且受尊敬的
definition_en: Famous and respected for achievements in a particular field.
example1_en: I copied internationally eminent into my lecture notes.
example1_zh: 我把享有国际盛誉的抄进了课堂笔记。
example2_en: Students compared two sources that both discuss internationally eminent.
example2_zh: 学生比较了两份都讨论享有国际盛誉的的材料。
collocations: eminent scholar｜杰出学者 ; eminent scientist｜著名科学家 ; internationally eminent｜享有国际盛誉的
tip_zh: eminent指杰出；imminent指即将发生。

meanings_zh: n. 配给量；定量口粮 | v. 定量供应；配给
definition_en: A fixed amount of food or supplies allowed to someone. | To limit how much of something each person can have.
example1_en: Our professor circled a daily ration on the slide.
example1_zh: 教授在幻灯片上圈出了每日配给量。
example2_en: The author returns to a daily ration when explaining the conclusion.
example2_zh: 作者在解释结论时又回到了每日配给量。
collocations: a daily ration｜每日配给量 ; food rations｜配给口粮 ; ration water｜定量供水
tip_zh: 作动词可用ration someone to，表示限量。

meanings_zh: n. 枢轴；支点 | v. 转动；转身 | v. 转变方向；调整策略
definition_en: A fixed point around which something turns. | To turn around a fixed point or on one foot. | To change direction, strategy, or focus.
example1_en: The textbook introduces a central pivot in the first chapter.
example1_zh: 教材在第一章介绍了中央枢轴。
example2_en: The listening passage defines the discussion around a central pivot.
example2_zh: 这段听力材料围绕中央枢轴展开说明。
collocations: a central pivot｜中央枢轴 ; pivot on one foot｜以一只脚为轴转身 ; pivot towards online services｜转向线上服务
tip_zh: pivotal 表示关键的；pivot 作动词也可指策略转向。

meanings_zh: n. 失眠；失眠症
definition_en: a condition involving difficulty falling asleep or staying asleep
example1_en: Our professor circled suffer from insomnia on the slide.
example1_zh: 教授在幻灯片上圈出了受失眠困扰。
example2_en: The reading connects suffer from insomnia with a larger point about public health.
example2_zh: 这篇阅读把受失眠困扰和关于公共卫生的一个更大的问题联系起来。
collocations: suffer from insomnia｜受失眠困扰 ; chronic insomnia｜慢性失眠 ; treat insomnia｜治疗失眠
tip_zh: insomnia是不可数名词，常与suffer from连用。

meanings_zh: n. 正式协议 | n. 一致；协调 | v. 给予；授予
definition_en: A formal agreement between countries, groups, or organisations. | Agreement or harmony between people, ideas, or actions. | To give someone respect, rights, or special treatment.
example1_en: The seminar spent a few minutes on accord equal rights.
example1_zh: 研讨课花了几分钟讨论给予平等权利。
example2_en: The author returns to accord equal rights when explaining the conclusion.
example2_zh: 作者在解释结论时又回到了给予平等权利。
collocations: reach an accord｜达成协议 ; in accord with｜与……一致 ; of your own accord｜自愿地 ; accord equal rights｜给予平等权利
tip_zh: of your own accord意为自愿地，无需别人要求。

meanings_zh: n. 美德；高尚品德 | n. 优点；长处
definition_en: A morally good quality or morally good behaviour. | A useful or desirable quality of something.
example1_en: The seminar spent a few minutes on moral virtue.
example1_zh: 研讨课花了几分钟讨论道德美德。
example2_en: The reading connects moral virtue with a larger point about social change.
example2_zh: 这篇阅读把道德美德和关于社会变迁的一个更大的问题联系起来。
collocations: moral virtue｜道德美德 ; the virtues of｜……的优点 ; by virtue of｜由于；凭借
tip_zh: by virtue of意为由于或凭借，并非凭美德。

meanings_zh: n. 波动；起伏
definition_en: A change in level or amount, especially up and down.
example1_en: I wrote fluctuation on a note card with its meaning.
example1_zh: 我把fluctuation和它的意思写在了笔记卡上。
example2_en: Students who can explain fluctuation usually follow the rest of a lecture on economic policy.
example2_zh: 能解释波动的学生，通常跟得上一节关于经济政策的讲座。
collocations: price fluctuations｜价格波动 ; seasonal fluctuations｜季节性波动 ; fluctuations in demand｜需求波动 ; temperature fluctuations｜温度波动
tip_zh: 常用fluctuations in加变化的指标，如prices。

meanings_zh: n. 欺骗；欺诈手段
definition_en: the act of deliberately making someone believe something false
example1_en: The quiz had a short question about deliberate deception.
example1_zh: 小测里有一道关于蓄意欺骗的简答题。
example2_en: In the lecture on social change, everyone remembered the example of deliberate deception.
example2_zh: 在关于社会变迁的讲座里，大家都记得蓄意欺骗这个例子。
collocations: deliberate deception｜蓄意欺骗 ; practise deception｜实施欺骗 ; an act of deception｜欺骗行为
tip_zh: deception强调故意使人信以为真，不是普通错误。

meanings_zh: adj. 鲜为人知的 | adj. 费解的；不清楚的 | v. 遮蔽；使模糊
definition_en: Not known by many people | Difficult to understand or not clearly expressed | Prevent something from being seen or understood clearly
example1_en: I copied an obscure writer into my lecture notes.
example1_zh: 我把鲜为人知的作家抄进了课堂笔记。
example2_en: The author returns to an obscure writer when explaining the conclusion.
example2_zh: 作者在解释结论时又回到了鲜为人知的作家。
collocations: an obscure writer｜鲜为人知的作家 ; an obscure reference｜难懂的典故 ; obscure the view｜遮挡视线 ; obscure the truth｜掩盖真相
tip_zh: 作形容词指无名或难懂；作动词指遮蔽或掩盖。

meanings_zh: n. 内部人士；知情者
definition_en: Someone within a group who has access to private information.
example1_en: The quiz had a short question about industry insider.
example1_zh: 小测里有一道关于业内人士的简答题。
example2_en: A campus survey used industry insider to explain a pattern in economic policy.
example2_zh: 一项校园调查用业内人士来解释经济政策中的一种模式。
collocations: industry insider｜业内人士 ; political insider｜政界内部人士 ; insider knowledge｜内部消息 ; insider trading｜内幕交易
tip_zh: 指因身处组织内部而掌握内情的人。

meanings_zh: v. 使失效；使作废 | v. 使不能成立
definition_en: to make something no longer legally or officially acceptable | to show that an argument or result is not sound
example1_en: In office hours we practiced how to invalidate a warranty.
example1_zh: 答疑时我们练习如何使保修失效。
example2_en: The passage says students who can invalidate a warranty follow the argument more easily.
example2_zh: 文章说，能够使保修失效的学生更容易跟上论点。
collocations: invalidate a warranty｜使保修失效 ; invalidate a contract｜使合同无效 ; invalidate the results｜使结果失去效力
tip_zh: 可指合同等正式失效，也可指证据使结论不能成立。

meanings_zh: v. 改编成戏剧 | v. 夸大；使戏剧化
definition_en: to adapt a story or event for performance | to present something as more exciting or serious than it is
example1_en: In office hours we practiced how to dramatize a novel.
example1_zh: 答疑时我们练习如何把小说改编成戏剧。
example2_en: A lecture on the humanities showed why researchers dramatize a novel before they publish.
example2_zh: 关于人文学科的讲座说明了研究者为什么在发表之前要把小说改编成戏剧。
collocations: dramatize a novel｜把小说改编成戏剧 ; dramatize historical events｜将历史事件改编成戏剧 ; dramatize a situation｜夸大情势
tip_zh: 英式也常拼作dramatise；可指改编，也可指夸大。

meanings_zh: n. 计算；计算过程
definition_en: The process of finding an answer using mathematics or computers.
example1_en: Office hours began with complex computation.
example1_zh: 答疑从复杂计算开始。
example2_en: In the lecture on technological change, everyone remembered the example of complex computation.
example2_zh: 在关于技术变革的讲座里，大家都记得复杂计算这个例子。
collocations: complex computation｜复杂计算 ; numerical computation｜数值计算 ; parallel computation｜并行计算 ; computation time｜计算时间
tip_zh: 比calculation更正式，常用于数学和计算机领域。

meanings_zh: adj. 强效的；有力的
definition_en: having a strong effect or powerful influence
example1_en: The quiz had a short question about potent drug.
example1_zh: 小测里有一道关于强效药物的简答题。
example2_en: In the lecture on the natural sciences, everyone remembered the example of potent drug.
example2_zh: 在关于自然科学的讲座里，大家都记得强效药物这个例子。
collocations: potent drug｜强效药物 ; potent symbol｜有力的象征 ; potent force｜强大的力量 ; potent reminder｜强烈的提醒
tip_zh: 强调效力或影响强，不等于potential“潜在的”。

meanings_zh: n. 涟漪；细小波纹 | v. 泛起涟漪；使起波纹 | n. 逐渐扩散的反应或影响
definition_en: A small wave on the surface of water. | To move in small waves or make something do so. | A reaction or effect that spreads through people or places.
example1_en: Office hours began with ripple effect.
example1_zh: 答疑从连锁效应开始。
example2_en: The reading connects ripple effect with a larger point about the natural sciences.
example2_zh: 这篇阅读把连锁效应和关于自然科学的一个更大的问题联系起来。
collocations: ripple effect｜连锁效应 ; ripples on the water｜水面上的涟漪 ; a ripple of laughter｜一阵轻轻传开的笑声
tip_zh: ripple比wave小；ripple effect指连锁效应。

meanings_zh: n. 海峡 | n. 困境；窘迫
definition_en: a narrow stretch of sea connecting two larger areas | a situation involving serious difficulty, especially lack of money
example1_en: Office hours began with a narrow strait.
example1_zh: 答疑从狭窄的海峡开始。
example2_en: The listening passage defines the discussion around a narrow strait.
example2_zh: 这段听力材料围绕狭窄的海峡展开说明。
collocations: a narrow strait｜狭窄的海峡 ; cross a strait｜穿过海峡 ; in dire straits｜陷入严重困境
tip_zh: 表示困境通常用复数straits，如in dire straits。

meanings_zh: n. 被排斥者；被遗弃者 | adj. 被排斥的；被遗弃的
definition_en: Someone rejected and excluded by a group or society. | Rejected and excluded by other people.
example1_en: Our professor circled a social outcast on the slide.
example1_zh: 教授在幻灯片上圈出了被社会排斥的人。
example2_en: The reading connects a social outcast with a larger point about social change.
example2_zh: 这篇阅读把被社会排斥的人和关于社会变迁的一个更大的问题联系起来。
collocations: a social outcast｜被社会排斥的人 ; feel like an outcast｜觉得自己被排斥 ; treat someone as an outcast｜把某人当作异类排斥
tip_zh: 主要作名词，指被排斥者，并不等于流浪者或流氓。

meanings_zh: adj. 可协商的 | adj. 可转让兑现的
definition_en: able to be changed through discussion and agreement | legally transferable to another person in exchange for money
example1_en: The seminar spent a few minutes on a negotiable price.
example1_zh: 研讨课花了几分钟讨论可商议的价格。
example2_en: Students compared two sources that both discuss a negotiable price.
example2_zh: 学生比较了两份都讨论可商议的价格的材料。
collocations: a negotiable price｜可商议的价格 ; negotiable terms｜可协商的条款 ; a negotiable salary｜可面议的薪资 ; a negotiable instrument｜可转让票据
tip_zh: 价格或条件可协商用negotiable；反义为non-negotiable。

meanings_zh: adj. 熟练的；精通的
definition_en: Able to do something well through training and practice.
example1_en: Our professor circled highly proficient on the slide.
example1_zh: 教授在幻灯片上圈出了非常熟练的。
example2_en: A campus survey used highly proficient to explain a pattern in economic policy.
example2_zh: 一项校园调查用非常熟练的来解释经济政策中的一种模式。
collocations: proficient in English｜英语熟练的 ; proficient at using software｜熟练使用软件的 ; highly proficient｜非常熟练的
tip_zh: 常用proficient in某领域或at某项活动。

meanings_zh: n. 大火；烈火 | v. 熊熊燃烧；强烈照耀
definition_en: a large, strong fire | to burn fiercely or shine very brightly
example1_en: I copied a forest blaze into my lecture notes.
example1_zh: 我把森林大火抄进了课堂笔记。
example2_en: A campus survey used a forest blaze to explain a pattern in environmental policy.
example2_zh: 一项校园调查用森林大火来解释环境政策中的一种模式。
collocations: fight a blaze｜扑救大火 ; a forest blaze｜森林大火 ; blaze a trail｜开辟道路；率先探索
tip_zh: blaze常指猛烈的大火；flame指火焰。

meanings_zh: n. 避难所；安宁之地
definition_en: a safe or peaceful place away from danger or trouble
example1_en: Office hours began with safe haven.
example1_zh: 答疑从安全避难所开始。
example2_en: In the lecture on environmental policy, everyone remembered the example of safe haven.
example2_zh: 在关于环境政策的讲座里，大家都记得安全避难所这个例子。
collocations: safe haven｜安全避难所 ; haven for wildlife｜野生动物的庇护所 ; haven of peace｜宁静之地
tip_zh: 常用a haven for；注意与heaven（天堂）区分。

meanings_zh: n. 暴政；专制统治 | n. 严酷控制；压迫
definition_en: cruel government that uses power without limits | cruel or unreasonable control over other people
example1_en: The textbook introduces resist tyranny in the first chapter.
example1_zh: 教材在第一章介绍了反抗暴政。
example2_en: The listening passage defines the discussion around resist tyranny.
example2_zh: 这段听力材料围绕反抗暴政展开说明。
collocations: resist tyranny｜反抗暴政 ; political tyranny｜政治暴政 ; the tyranny of the majority｜多数人的暴政
tip_zh: 强调权力的残酷滥用，比一般的严格管理更严重。

meanings_zh: v. 召唤；传唤 | v. 鼓起；振作
definition_en: To officially order someone to come or request their presence. | To gather the courage, strength, or energy needed for something.
example1_en: I heard the lecturer summon help during the example.
example1_zh: 我听到讲者在举例时叫人来帮忙。
example2_en: The reading asks you to summon help and then check a second source.
example2_zh: 这篇阅读要求你叫人来帮忙，然后再核对第二个来源。
collocations: summon someone to court｜传唤某人出庭 ; summon help｜叫人来帮忙 ; summon up courage｜鼓起勇气
tip_zh: summon sb to某处；summon up courage指鼓起勇气。

meanings_zh: n. 怨恨；愤懑 | n. 苦味
definition_en: Anger and resentment caused by unfair treatment or disappointment. | A sharp, unpleasant taste like unsweetened coffee.
example1_en: The quiz had a short question about lasting bitterness.
example1_zh: 小测里有一道关于持久的怨恨的简答题。
example2_en: A campus survey used lasting bitterness to explain a pattern in human behavior.
example2_zh: 一项校园调查用持久的怨恨来解释人类行为中的一种模式。
collocations: feel bitterness｜感到怨恨 ; lasting bitterness｜持久的怨恨 ; the bitterness of coffee｜咖啡的苦味
tip_zh: 通常不可数；既指味觉上的苦，也指内心怨恨。

meanings_zh: v. 委托；托付
definition_en: To give someone responsibility for something or someone valuable.
example1_en: The assignment is to entrust someone with a task, then say why it matters.
example1_zh: 作业是先委托某人执行任务，再说明它为什么重要。
example2_en: A lecture on economic policy showed why researchers entrust someone with a task before they publish.
example2_zh: 关于经济政策的讲座说明了研究者为什么在发表之前要委托某人执行任务。
collocations: entrust someone with a task｜委托某人执行任务 ; entrust something to someone｜把某物托付给某人 ; entrust someone with responsibility｜委以某人重任
tip_zh: entrust人with物；entrust物to人。

meanings_zh: n. 捕鲸；捕鲸业
definition_en: the activity or business of hunting whales
example1_en: Office hours began with commercial whaling.
example1_zh: 答疑从商业捕鲸开始。
example2_en: The author returns to commercial whaling when explaining the conclusion.
example2_zh: 作者在解释结论时又回到了商业捕鲸。
collocations: commercial whaling｜商业捕鲸 ; whaling ship｜捕鲸船 ; whaling industry｜捕鲸业 ; ban on whaling｜捕鲸禁令
tip_zh: 不可数名词；谈捕鲸禁令用ban on whaling。

meanings_zh: n. 礼堂；会堂 | n. 观众席
definition_en: a large room or building for an audience | the part of a theatre where the audience sits
example1_en: The seminar spent a few minutes on school auditorium.
example1_zh: 研讨课花了几分钟讨论学校礼堂。
example2_en: The listening passage defines the discussion around school auditorium.
example2_zh: 这段听力材料围绕学校礼堂展开说明。
collocations: school auditorium｜学校礼堂 ; main auditorium｜主礼堂 ; packed auditorium｜座无虚席的礼堂
tip_zh: 可指整座礼堂，也可专指剧院的观众席。

meanings_zh: n. 资历；年资 | n. 级别较高；地位较高
definition_en: The advantage or status gained from longer service. | The state of holding a higher rank than others.
example1_en: The quiz had a short question about based on seniority.
example1_zh: 小测里有一道关于以资历为依据的简答题。
example2_en: The author returns to based on seniority when explaining the conclusion.
example2_zh: 作者在解释结论时又回到了以资历为依据。
collocations: based on seniority｜以资历为依据 ; years of seniority｜任职年资 ; seniority system｜年资制度
tip_zh: 不可数；主要指任职资历或职级，不只是年龄。

meanings_zh: v. 证实；为……提供证据
definition_en: to provide evidence showing that something is true
example1_en: The assignment is to substantiate a claim, then say why it matters.
example1_zh: 作业是先证实一项主张，再说明它为什么重要。
example2_en: In the sample listening, the professor pauses to substantiate a claim.
example2_zh: 在示例听力里，教授停下来证实一项主张。
collocations: substantiate a claim｜证实一项主张 ; substantiate an allegation｜证实一项指控 ; substantiate with evidence｜用证据证实
tip_zh: 正式及物动词；后接claim等，强调拿出证据。

meanings_zh: n. 独白 | n. 滔滔不绝的独自讲话
definition_en: A long speech delivered by one character in a performance. | A long speech by someone who gives others little chance to speak.
example1_en: The seminar spent a few minutes on a dramatic monologue.
example1_zh: 研讨课花了几分钟讨论戏剧独白。
example2_en: The reading connects a dramatic monologue with a larger point about the humanities.
example2_zh: 这篇阅读把戏剧独白和关于人文学科的一个更大的问题联系起来。
collocations: deliver a monologue｜表演一段独白 ; a dramatic monologue｜戏剧独白 ; an interior monologue｜内心独白
tip_zh: 独白可对观众说，不一定是角色自言自语。

meanings_zh: n. 高原 | n. 平台期；稳定水平 | v. 进入平台期；趋于稳定
definition_en: A large area of flat land higher than surrounding land. | A period when growth or progress stops after an increase. | To stop increasing or improving and remain at a steady level.
example1_en: Office hours began with a high plateau.
example1_zh: 答疑从高原开始。
example2_en: A campus survey used a high plateau to explain a pattern in the natural sciences.
example2_zh: 一项校园调查用高原来解释自然科学中的一种模式。
collocations: a high plateau｜高原 ; reach a plateau｜进入平台期 ; a learning plateau｜学习平台期
tip_zh: 平台期指增长后趋稳，不表示水平开始下降。

meanings_zh: n. 承认；认可 | n. 致谢；鸣谢 | n. 收悉通知；回执
definition_en: Acceptance that something is true or that someone's contribution matters. | An expression of thanks for help or support. | A message confirming that something has been received.
example1_en: The textbook introduces public acknowledgment in the first chapter.
example1_zh: 教材在第一章介绍了公开承认。
example2_en: The listening passage defines the discussion around public acknowledgment.
example2_zh: 这段听力材料围绕公开承认展开说明。
collocations: in acknowledgment of｜为认可；为感谢 ; acknowledgment of receipt｜收悉确认 ; public acknowledgment｜公开承认 ; an acknowledgment of support｜对支持的感谢
tip_zh: 英式也常拼acknowledgement；各义常接of。

meanings_zh: n. 参数 | n. 限定条件；范围
definition_en: A measurable factor used to describe a system or calculation. | A limit or condition controlling how something can be done.
example1_en: Our professor circled key parameter on the slide.
example1_zh: 教授在幻灯片上圈出了关键参数。
example2_en: In the lecture on the natural sciences, everyone remembered the example of key parameter.
example2_zh: 在关于自然科学的讲座里，大家都记得关键参数这个例子。
collocations: key parameter｜关键参数 ; set parameters｜设定参数或范围 ; within the parameters｜在限定范围内
tip_zh: 表限定条件时常用复数；勿与周长perimeter混淆。

meanings_zh: n. 宏观经济学
definition_en: The study of whole economies, including growth, inflation, and unemployment.
example1_en: The seminar spent a few minutes on principles of macroeconomics.
example1_zh: 研讨课花了几分钟讨论宏观经济学原理。
example2_en: In the lecture on economic policy, everyone remembered the example of principles of macroeconomics.
example2_zh: 在关于经济政策的讲座里，大家都记得宏观经济学原理这个例子。
collocations: study macroeconomics｜学习宏观经济学 ; macroeconomics course｜宏观经济学课程 ; principles of macroeconomics｜宏观经济学原理
tip_zh: 虽以s结尾，指学科时接单数谓语；区别于微观经济学。

meanings_zh: n. 不一致；前后矛盾 | n. 不稳定；时好时坏
definition_en: a lack of agreement between facts, statements, or actions | the quality of varying unpredictably in standard or performance
example1_en: I copied internal inconsistency into my lecture notes.
example1_zh: 我把内部矛盾抄进了课堂笔记。
example2_en: In the lecture on academic research, everyone remembered the example of internal inconsistency.
example2_zh: 在关于学术研究的讲座里，大家都记得内部矛盾这个例子。
collocations: inconsistency between accounts｜叙述之间的矛盾 ; internal inconsistency｜内部矛盾 ; inconsistency in performance｜表现不稳定
tip_zh: 可数时指一处矛盾；不可数时指不一致的状态。

meanings_zh: adj. 善于清晰表达的 | v. 清楚表达
